_comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for 'which firmware build includes which feature'. Derived from firmware/canary/platformio.ini (per-env -DFEATURE_* lines) + firmware/canary/include/canary_config.h (the #ifndef defaults) + firmware/flavors.json (which products/envs ship) + firmware/boards/boards.json (board tiers). Pinned by scripts/lint_build_matrix.py (CI) so it can't drift from the real feature flags, and mirrored into the securacv_website onboarding-spec.json (`builds`) so the /checkup firmware-type selector matches what each build actually does. IMPORTANT: only the `canary` (ESP32-S3) product carries dev/release/full LEVELS; the other products are single-level board-specialized builds. FEATURES.md is a human narrative that reports the SUPERSET capability and can lag — trust platformio.ini per level, not the dashboard ticks.

mesh.label: Fleet mesh
mesh.note: Peers + identify pulse. Full build only.

bluetooth.label: Bluetooth (BLE GATT)
bluetooth.note: NimBLE status service. Full build only — doesn't fit the dev/release OTA slots.

levels.dev: Debug channel: -Og, verbose logs, all sensing on, BLE off. Official esp32 core (2.x), partitions_ota.csv (1.9 MB A/B slots). GitHub prerelease channel.
levels.release: Shipping channel: -Os, quiet logs, sensing on, BLE off. Official core (2.x), partitions_ota.csv. This is the image release devices pull (built as release_ha, adds Home Assistant MQTT).
levels.full: Superset / WAP-parity: everything on incl. BLE + mesh + RF/chirp. Requires pioarduino core-3.x + default_8MB.csv (2×3.2 MB) — NimBLE 2.x needs core 3.x and overflows the smaller OTA slots, which is why BLE is full-only.

products.name: Canary · ESP32-CAM
products.note: Reach port (docs/strategy/30): the most-owned camera board there is. Keeps camera PEEK + Wi-Fi CSI + SD; no mic (none onboard, no free pins), no GPS, and no die-temp gauge — classic ESP32 has no supported tsens path, so the thermal tile would be a false reading rather than a missing one. USB-flashable only: no OTA channel until a Hardware Test Report promotes the board.

products.name: Canary · ESP32 DevKit
products.note: Reach port (docs/strategy/30): the plain ESP32 in the drawer. A Wi-Fi CSI presence witness with the signed chain — no camera, no mic, no SD slot (the witness log lives in flash), no die-temp gauge. GPS is available on the free UART2 with an external module. USB-flashable only until benched.

products.name: Canary · Freenove S3
products.note: Reach port (docs/strategy/30): the S3 camera kit most people are shipped. Camera on the Espressif S3-EYE map. No mic; SD is off because the slot is wired 1-bit SDMMC (no DAT3/CS routed) and the storage driver is SPI-mode — the witness log lives in flash. USB-flashable only until benched.

products.name: Canary Vision
products.mcu: ESP32-C3 host + Grove Vision AI V2
products.note: Camera lives on the Himax co-processor (loaded via SenseCraft), not the ESP host — the canary camera/SD/CSI feature tiles don't apply. USB-Serial console only.

products.name: Canary Sense
products.note: 60 GHz radar presence board. No camera / SD / CSI / BLE, and no battery or temperature reading either — it's a mains-powered witness. USB-Serial console only; end-to-end bench validation pending.
products._provenance: Why this lane lists only 'selftest' (corrected 2026-09-05; it used to claim 'battery' and 'thermal', which the /checkup page rendered as lit 'Battery' and 'Thermal / die temp' pills for the ESP32-C6 auto-pick): the firmware has neither. FEATURE_POWER_MONITOR and FEATURE_DIAGNOSTICS appear nowhere in firmware/configs/canary-sense/, firmware/projects/canary-sense/ or firmware/envs/platformio/canary-sense.ini; src/net/fleet_beacon_adv.cpp sends battery_pct as 0xFF/unknown with the comment 'mains-powered witness, no battery gauge'; publish_health_retained() in src/net/mqtt_mgr.cpp hardcodes "battery":100 with "battery_present":false; and a case-insensitive grep for temperature/temp_c/tsens across the project returns nothing. firmware/FEATURES.md agrees (the canary-sense cell on the battery row is not-applicable). Fields prefixed with _ are monorepo-only: scripts/carry_to_site.py projects a field whitelist, so this does not reach the website.

products.name: Canary Watch Station
products.note: The canary-display lane: a fleet VIEWER, not a witness. It renders and verifies what the Canaries publish (TOFU-pinned Ed25519 chain heads, MQTT + HA discovery, signed pull-OTA with an HA update entity), records no witness chain of its own, and has no camera, mic, CSI, GPS or SD witness log — so none of the sensing tiles apply. 'selftest' here is the OTA engine's post-update boot self-test (rollback safety), not the canary tree's 10-probe suite. The watch (XIAO ESP32-S3 + Seeed Round Display, flavors.json check_env) stands for the line; the other display products are the same firmware on other glass, listed in canary-local/devices/flash.json and flavors.json release_envs. USB-flashable and OTA-published; the hardware tier stays compile-tested until a Hardware Test Report promotes a board.

recommended._comment: What the /checkup page and the flasher pick BY DEFAULT so the user doesn't have to. `default` is the pick when nothing is known (no board plugged in): the verified S3 all-rounder on the shipping channel. `forChip` is the pick once the flasher detects the silicon in hand. The board×level matrix stays available as a developer/education option. Pinned by lint_build_matrix.py.
recommended.why: The all-rounder witness — full sensing plus the Home Assistant bridge — on the verified S3, shipping channel. If you're not sure, this is the one.

flasher._comment: The /checkup 'Flash in browser' button deep-links here as flash.html?product=securacv-<id>. Each build_matrix product id maps to the flasher catalog product 'securacv-<id>' in canary-local/devices/flash.json; scripts/lint_build_matrix.py enforces that every mapping resolves, so renaming a flasher product breaks CI instead of the button. Flashing installs the signed RELEASE image for the board (levels are a feature-visibility axis, not separate flasher products) — that keeps it to four curated choices, not a build per level.

provenance.featureCatalog: firmware/canary/platformio.ini per-env -DFEATURE_* + firmware/canary/include/canary_config.h #ifndef defaults (FEATURE_DIAGNOSTICS=1, FEATURE_BLE_STATUS base 0 / full 1, FEATURE_MESH_NETWORK full only, FEATURE_TEST_CONSOLE never set)
provenance.products: firmware/flavors.json (build_envs per product; release_envs for the display board envs the release publishes) + firmware/boards/boards.json (board id, mcu, tier, used_by)
provenance.manifests: firmware/scripts/ota_release.py + docs/firmware_ota.md · per-variant manifest-<product>.json at releases/latest/download/; manifest-index.json lists all products
provenance.lint: scripts/lint_build_matrix.py — pins the load-bearing cells (BLE full-only, TEST_CONSOLE never shipped, DIAGNOSTICS always, sense/vision serial-only) to platformio.ini + canary_config.h, and requires a lane for every flavors.json product
